mappings.note: Plain kaavyabodh recall of whom the gopis love; not LO-7, nothing aesthetic is asked.
Recall of who is called 'badbhaagi'; the irony is not asked here, so not LO-7.
Content recall from the pad; no figure of speech named, so not LO-5.
Attribution of the pad to its poet is literary knowledge, not kaavyabodh of the text; LO-6 rejected.
Who is called abala/bholi - straight comprehension, not the bhaav-paksh analysis of LO-7.
Recall of the object of the gopis' attachment; not LO-7, no image is being interpreted.
Which message Uddhav brought - factual comprehension of the pad.
Names the alankaar in 'jog sandesani suni-suni' (punarukti prakash); LO-5 is the only alankaar outcome, so not LO-7.
Whom the gopis wish to appeal to - comprehension, not appreciation.
Effect of the message on their vyatha; asks what happened, not how it is rendered, so not LO-7.
Whose unspoken words stayed unspoken - content recall.
Identifies anupras in 'avadhi adhaar aas aavan ki'; an alankaar item, so LO-5 not LO-7.
What the gopis were told would happen - comprehension of the pad's narrative.
Turns on which upamaan the poet did NOT use for yoga; that is kala-paksh imagery, not plain recall (LO-6).
Whose talk was called kadvi kakdi - recall of what the image attaches to, not an analysis of it.
What is called a disease - comprehension; the metaphor itself is not being appraised.
For whom yoga is useful - the pad's argument, so kaavyabodh rather than LO-7 appreciation.
Asks what the 'kaanh-kaanh' line expresses - bhaav-paksh, not factual recall (LO-6).
Referent of 'tinahin' inside the pad - comprehension of the line, not its aesthetic.

Who is said to be doing parhit - content recall of the taunt's target.
Who is 'pahle se chatur' - comprehension; the sarcasm is not what is asked.
Whose welfare the ancients sought - straight comprehension of the pad.
Who stole the gopis' hearts - factual recall, not LO-7.
What Krishna practised toward the gopis (aneeti) - comprehension of the charge.
Identifies not troubling the praja as raajdharm - the pad's stated idea, so LO-6.
Asks who is satirised by whom; vyangya is kala-paksh, not the factual recall of LO-6.
Who stayed untouched by Krishna's love despite his company - comprehension.
The kamal-patta comparison for Uddhav's detachment is an upamaan; LO-7 rather than plain recall.
Where Krishna went (Mathura) - factual comprehension.
How the gopis find Krishna's conduct - stated in the pad, so comprehension not appreciation.
What the gopis call themselves - direct recall.
Object of the gopis' attachment - comprehension of the pad.

Who broke the maryada of love - comprehension of the accusation.
Who carried the yoga message - factual recall.
Who carried off their hearts - factual recall; duplicate of an earlier stem but mapped on its own terms.
Surdas's idea of true raajdharm as stated in the pad - kaavyabodh.

Names Krishna's friend who brings the message - comprehension of the pad's cast.
Who calls Uddhav badbhaagi - recall of the speaker, not of the irony (LO-7).
Toward whom the gopis express love - comprehension.
'Preeti-nadi' is a roopak; asking its referent is kala-paksh interpretation, so LO-7 not LO-6.
'Gur chaanti jyaun paagi' - reading the gud image as Krishna's love is figurative interpretation, LO-7.
Plain paraphrase of 'man ki man hi maanjh rahi'; a meaning gloss, not an aesthetic appraisal.
What the gopis wanted to say and to whom - comprehension.
Whom they think of day and night - factual recall.
Asks what 'kadvi kakdi' stands for; interpreting the pratik is LO-7, unlike item 15 which asked whose words they were.
'Man chakri' abhipray - reading the simile of the spinning top, so kala-paksh not LO-6.
'Byadhi' as a metaphor for yoga sadhana; figurative referent, LO-7.
Who learned raajneeti per the gopis - comprehension. Item is typed very_short but carries wrapped MCQ options in its stem.
Asks what vyangya lies in calling Uddhav fortunate - explicitly an irony question, so LO-7 not LO-6.
How ananya prem is expressed - manner of expression is bhaav-paksh, so LO-7.
Why 'hari hain raajneeti padh aae' was said - the barb behind the line, vyangya, so LO-7 over LO-6.
How yoga seems to them and who really needs it - the pad's content, kaavyabodh.
To whom yoga should be taught - comprehension of the gopis' retort.
Asks what they compare themselves to and why - upamaan plus its justification, kala-paksh.
Which maryada 'marjada na lahi' refers to - a meaning gloss, so LO-6 rather than LO-7.
Why they call themselves abala and bholi - reasoning from the text, not an aesthetic appraisal.
Which raajneeti they see in Krishna's conduct - comprehension of the charge.
